claims.text: Reducing FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbon width below a critical threshold increases the density of edge-induced defects.
Edge-induced defects in the nanoribbons act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Structural defects and microstructural discontinuities can impede domain-wall motion.
Defect-induced domain-wall pinning increases coercivity or magnetic hysteresis.
Narrower ribbons have a larger proportion of edge regions than wider ribbons or unpatterned films.
Lithographic processing introduces defects at nanoribbon edges.
Increasing edge-defect pinning reduces the effective magnetocaloric response and magnetocaloric entropy change.
FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons below a critical width will have greater magnetic hysteresis than unpatterned films or wider ribbons.
FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons below a critical width will have a smaller magnetocaloric entropy change than unpatterned films or wider ribbons.
The relevant magnetic transition temperature of the proposed FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons is around room temperature.
The proposed width-dependent mechanism is expected to govern behavior under applied fields below 50 Oe.
Additional lithographic damage beyond edge effects could confound the relationship between ribbon width and magnetic behavior.
The critical width and magnitude of magnetocaloric suppression depend on the lithographic process and resulting defect structure.

Failure to observe both increasing hysteresis and decreasing magnetocaloric response with decreasing width, or failure to observe a correlation with edge-defect density, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
